distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment improves significantly the longer they play, shifting from frustration during the opening hours to high praise among experienced players.

citations.review_text: no game all dialogue, 20 to 30 minutes per npc who wants you to run the to other side of the map, where youll be treated to 5 npc's along the way that will do the same thing, youll look desperatly for fun but the gameplay is poor and  clunky is being generous, this should have been a novel and stayed as one

Yea, this game is not for me. 
I don't need to mention the good parts (of which there are plenty), but the game ist just so dull for me. 
The combat system is system is absolutely horrific. Maybe I dont understand it, as I did not play the first part, but the game makes no attempt at explaining anything. There is a 2 min fight in full armor during the Into, afterwards you are dropped into a world where absolutely everything kills you with 2-3 hits, as you run around basically naked. 
You run out of stamina after 2 swings, or blocks. I can shoot 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ arrows in someones face and they continue to kill me in seconds anyway.  
After each fight (in the rare case you survive) you have to work on getting heathy again. also you have to repair all your stuff, and gather food. 
The game is basically a work simulator. I already have a job, thanks. 
There might people who enjoy the hyper realism... I dont..
Dialogue is boring, Combat is clunky, movement is clunky, everything is tedious.

Don't bother with this one there is a massive issue with it. I played through the messy combat of the original and completed it with only a few issues but it was a good game. Now in the sequel there is just something off where the supposedly improved combat doesn't work and often forces you into long chains of attacks against perfect guards not allowing you to block or change attack direction and even if you get an ambush off against a bandit and mollywop them 3-4 times they attack back at full health and stamina. 

I barely got out of the starting village and several bandits accosting some man at arms soldier at the crossroads all switched off target and came after me causing me to have to go back 15 minutes and try again only to find it was a basic random encounter, I am currently stuck in the forest trying to deal with a single cumen who is unkillable who 2-3 shot kills me everytime no matter how well I parry and get hits in on him because they simply do not count for damage and after 10 solid hits with blood he is perfectly fine. Absolutely impossible and punishing.

So I have tried to do this fight another 20 times and I finally  got into a perfect block/riposte chain that was up to 10 swings before I was instantly killed and could not land a single hit as they would make little dodges or counter parries that I would then block and counter and I would just miss. If anyone knows how to turn the games cheating off or player cheating on let me know. This is absolutely absurd. I finally just deleted the save and will maybe try again later.

I'm genuinely shocked at how terrible the combat is. I was expecting something like mount and blade, for honor, chivalry or mordhau. But it's a far cry from anything competently made. Directional blocking actually doesn't matter, ripostes are useless, lock on system is a mess for multiple opponents. Most surprisingly of all, the combat is slow and clunky to the point of being comically unrealistic. You also don't really get many opportunities to test out the combat until you are well past the 2 hour refund period.

A generally fun game with some flaws.

The story, exploration and general world building is fantastic and it is a game with a lot of content which will keep you busy.
The potion and blacksmithing minigames are generally fine but they get tedious after a while. 
The biggest issue is the combat system. It is clunky and simply annoying at times (especially with saving being tied to sleeping / potion). You will get jumped by either bandits or wolves and you will die. a lot. but when you aren't dying, the game is very enjoyable.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that saving progress requires specific items or conditions like sleeping, which can cause significant loss of progress upon death.

citations.review_text: I really tried to enjoy this game, I have a lot of issues with it. Maybe one day I will revisit it. I can tell the story is good, and that the devs care about this game but I simply have lost too much time dying and being sent back over 20 minutes and having to repeat content. There's hardly an autosave and needing to craft something to save is insane. Combat wasn't rewarding in my experience, but I can tell I would've eventually enjoyed it but needing to constantly repair armor/weapons when practicing with Tomcat was a big turn off for me. There's a lot of good things, and if you have a lot of time, are very difficult to dissuade  and want an incredibly deep RPG this might be a good game for you. But to me it just felt like an overly complex chore simulator 60% of the time, slow methodical combat 10% of the time and the other 30% of the time you're doing all the chores you just did again.

This game fights you at every possible chance in order to make the experience as artificially difficult as possible. The game is unintuitive in so many ways, the combat system is intriguing but chooses to be weirdly difficult in its scaling to a point that it feels unfair. The game does nothing to guide you away from these problems, to the point that they feel intentional. The rain looks absolutely horrendous, it's actually crazy. The game presents stealth encounters like they are a thing that you are meant to do, but when trying to stealth kill the game just chooses to not let it happen despite what feels like a proper character level and equipment while also doing the quick time event. You can just randomly run into a pack of wolves or something of the like with no forewarning and then you just die because a group fight in this game is a death sentence. In fact most areas that you are not allowed in give you no warning of this and if you are moving fast then suddenly you are in a fight, which often leads to an immediate death. You need a potion to save if you aren't at your bed, which would be negligible if not for the aforementioned problems about how combat and random encounters are extremely punishing. The game teaches you ripostes like they are this important thing at the start, but you immediately learn that it is the most useless mechanic ever as all enemies, even ones at the start of the game are parry gods and your riposte counterattack is at best cosmetic. All in all the game sucks and its a skill issue.

Game has been solid so far. Savior Schnapps has to be the most rage inducing game mechanic ever. How disappointing. At least make Belladona less rare. I can't find anywhere and I have not ran into any traders with it. I am resorting to installing a saving mod from the workshop because the program managers leading this game couldn't get over their ego. I cannot recommend the game unless the saving mechanism gets an overhaul.
this game has no respect for my time. im 36, ill die soon, dont make me mix potions every step. save system sucks, combat is clunky to me. oh well

Henry is a lovable character. The game is beautiful and the music is absolutely brilliant (probably in my top ten video game soundtracks of all time). 

I understand and appreciate what the developers were trying to do with this game, but it's not for me. I don't have a ton of time to game, so getting stuck in endless loops of mediocre engagement with overly tedious mechanics that don't really have much impact on immersion or the story or really much of anything just isn't particularly enjoyable. I'm sure people with plenty of time on their hands who find sharpening swords, eating, washing clothes after every fight, and mastering the loopy combat system to be engaging and enjoyable. I do not. I realized after less than six hours of game time and spending an entire hour looking for mods to improve my experience that if I'm having to mod a game this early on just to enjoy it then I need to spend my time elsewhere.

Bought it thinking I'd be a fearless medieval knight.

Eight hours later I'm apologising to a blacksmith because I accidentally stole a cabbage, bleeding to death after losing a fistfight to a bloke called "Peasant", and sleeping until morning because walking through the woods at night seems like a ♥♥♥♥ idea.

I've spent more time washing blood off my clothes than I have in some RPGs' main stories.

10/10. Nothing has made me fear three angry villagers with sticks quite like this game.

Granted, I have only played four hours, but I can't seem to figure out the combat at even a basic level without re-reading the tutorial, I don't know where to go for quests as not all quests have markers, the menus are slow and cluttered, stamina is a pain to manage... this is just too much work and not enough fun and I wish I hadn't bought it as someone with not that much time for games these days.

I tried to get into the game. Spent 15 hours trying to get into it. Couldn't do it.

The whole quest and social system feels like its built on sand- ready to crumble/bug out at any moment. This feeling proved accurate during a rescue mission quest which mysteriously solved itself while I was bumbling about, lost in the woods. I don't know if it was set to solve itself after a timer, or if it was a bug. 

That's the other thing that I didn't like, was the fact that I had no idea where to go for any of the quests. I had to keep a hawk's eye on my map constantly to make sure that I was going in the right direction, and couldn't actually look around the world, which is the game's most redeeming aspect. 

The environment is gorgeous and detailed, and runs smooth as butter. It's just a shame that the game systems suck so much it's not fun to do anything in it.

The combat was also a huge slog, and did absolutely not feel good. I typically prefer faster-paced action RPGs nowadays, but I am well versed in the first person genre, having grown up in the Elder Scrolls series. By comparison, the combat in this game is at the bottom.

The rage-quit moment for me was after spending more than an hour trying over and over again to take out a bandit camp with about 4 opponents in it. I finally got all four of them (the last bandit ran away and made me chase him halfway across the valley.) Then, I go back, loot the camp, find a bunch of goodies, and spend the next half hour outfitting myself in all the spoils of war. I switch my outfit to something non-combatant; to stroll into town with style after a hard fight. Just as I'm about to head out and turn in my quest objective, a random bowman appears and pulls me off my horse. I can't fight back, since I changed out of my combat gear, and he proceeds to kill me and send me back to my save point just before entering the bandit camp- an hour and a half ago. 

I'm not wasting anymore time on this game.
Give it a shot if you wa…

This game systems are entirely clunky in every regard, so much so I have to assume that is "as intended". I don't need yellow paint or quest markers, but it's very strange that the 'game' is basically underexplained unless you run to reddit or youtube to get someone's tutorial.

I get that for some people that's a desirable experience. But there feels like a real lack of clarity in-game for why you're failing skill checks. Basically, it boils down to that you shouldn't progress quest lines until you've spent sufficient time doing miscellaneous stuff to blindly level up. 

The game is gorgeous. The story is compelling. But the actual mechanics are unclear and intentionally frictional to appeal to someone looking for a 'suffering simulator' (that is, unless they want to spoil the game discovery by reading reddit, etc). So, if you play the game honestly, you'll be repeating lots and lots and lots of interactions to make any progress, which ruins the narrative unfolding of the story. 

So, I've already played ~10 hours so I can't refund this, but I also can't play the game without leaning on spoilers to advance. I want to like it, A LOT, but replaying the same fight or interaction 20 times, reloading constantly, it's just not how I want to spend my free time. For that, this game is an utter failure.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game players encounter technical bugs and challenging combat, but appreciate the well-optimized performance, reactive open world, and detailed environment.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as well-optimized, noting it runs smoothly and performs well on various hardware configurations including mid-range setups and older graphics cards.

citations.review_text:
One of the best story games I have ever played.
Surprisingly, its very well optimised for GTX 1650 as well. 
Had an amazing experience with this game.
Highly recommended!!!!!!!

Hands down one of the best games I have ever played. The developers also did an amazing job optimizing the game's graphics and performance to look and run outstandingly on even mid-range hardware like mine. Jesus Christ be praised!

Performance:
Played for 77 hours on a GTX 1660 Ti. I kept all settings on Low and experienced absolutely zero crashes or stutters. If you are hesitating to buy this because of hardware limitations, don't. The game is perfectly playable, and the narrative easily overshadows any graphical compromises.

The Story & Characters:
Just like the first game, KCD2 is an absolute triumph in RPG storytelling. However, the true brilliance of this game lies in its supporting cast and antagonists. Markvart von Aulitz, Dry Devil, Janosh Uher, and Adder completely steal the show. Markvart commands every scene he is in, and his fate carries real narrative weight.

On the flip side, I grew completely exhausted with Henry's presence as the game dragged on. Worse was being forced to play as Godwin. While I understood the temporary narrative necessity of it—especially right after Zizka’s ambush on Henry and Capon, or handling the initial dialogues with Hanush—Godwin is simply an insufferable character to pilot.

World & Gameplay:
I treated this strictly as a story-driven experience. I ignored most side quests unless I was in the mood to level up skills or steal during the main campaign downtime.

The Verdict:
For me, the true ending of this game was my final dialogue with Markvart von Aulitz. Once the main narrative concludes, the open world becomes a completely empty stage. I opened the game twice after finishing it, stood around for a few minutes, and closed it. The sandbox means nothing without the story driving it.

Come for the incredible writing and complex characters, but don't expect to stay once the curtain falls. Highly recommended for the plot alone.

50+ hours in and this is already one of my favourite games OF ALL TIME. 

Playing KCD2 feels as close as I will get to living out my dream of being a proper Medieval knight.

Storyline is fantastic - there are so many twists and turns that I am already looking forward to my second playthrough before I have even finished my first...  

The Landscape and environments are beautiful, which makes it insanely immersive.

Combat is really tricky and almost frustrating at first - I was dying a LOT - but after watching a couple of youtube tutorials, it makes a lot more sense. (Don't spam ripostes, learn the masterstrike, and keep an eye on your stamina most of all) Once you wrap your head around it, and get good, it is incredibly satisfying. 

Oh and by the way, the game is super optimised, I am running it on my old 1080, and it is running beautifully. 

Just get this game already, it's a masterpiece.
great game optimized good running on 1440p High-Ultra in betwenn at 80-90 fps and amazing story

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering game-breaking bugs, softlocks, and technical issues during specific missions or region transitions.

citations.review_text: After playing for 50h, I'm spending more time trying to fix the memory leak bug which crashes the game, rather then actually playing it. Aside from that, for me, the game is less optimized than the first KCD which is a feat in itself.

It's an amazing game and the most immersive rpg there is. the alchemy and combat is addictingly fun. But even after a year of being out, there are STILL game breaking bugs and softlocks that can set you back hours of gameplay. For christ's sake fix the storm mission.

The base game feels like an expansion pack for the first one, barring a few cool quality of life improvements.
The DLCs are where it really opens up. The forge one is a must-have for me so far.
The biggest downside of the game are some of the missions: there are a few bugged ones, including a main quest "Blacksmith's son" and quite a lot of missions are very tedious. You are incentivised to look up online guides or forums to save the time and trouble of getting stuck, searching for something, interviewing NPCs or hauling bags/corpses. An example of a broken quest is being unable to raid a stash with a unique thief's cap because I did things out of order, so I had to google how to spawn this item with a console command. Immersion breaking to say the least ;D
Overall a great RPG game if you enjoy the combat controls and don't mind googling for solutions.

I think most people read reviews to find negative stuff (except devs, if they do), so I will mostly write about it))) Putting aside following issues, the game is a masterpiece!

Performance
-----------
- The game is VERY CPU-INTENSIVE. I spent a lot of time tweaking performance-related console commands to no avail and nearly gave up. If you're experiencing low GPU utilization (and FPS), disable hyperthreading in your BIOS. THIS BOOSTED FPS AND STABILITY A LOT (near 60 in the city, compared to ~35 before).
- If you experience crashes when traveling between regions (which you will do rarely), clear your shader cache and disable your user.cfg for a while.

Gameplay
--------
- It would be nice to have more difficulty settings (currently, there are only "Normal" and "Hardcore").
- Combat becomes much less challenging in the late game. The wiki says it's better in "Hardcore," but I would rather play on "Normal" with tougher enemies than switch to "Hardcore" with all its disruptive features. Consequently, tournaments and random encounters become less interesting.

In general, the game is great and definitely worth playing!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as challenging and unintuitive, noting that enemies can easily block attacks or defeat the player while stamina management and timing are strictly required.

citations.review_text: combat is actually awful. block promt>1/5 chance it works... you have the stamina of a wheelchair bound toddler. your armor and weapons can be 10 times better then the npcs yet you take 3-5 hits to die and they take 47. they can block as much as they want... you can block maybe 3 times. you also go through a pair of shoes daily.....................

KCD 2 is a top-tier RPG. Here are my impressions, broken down into pros and cons:

Pros:
+ A truly immersive world.
+ Gorgeous graphics. The vegetation, dirt roads, and medieval architecture are particularly well executed.
+ Excellent storytelling.
+ Top-notch voice acting (played with German audio).
+ The combat system can be a lot of fun and fits the setting perfectly. Especially early on, even a single bandit can give you a really hard time.
+ Beautifully designed UI (inventory, map, etc.).
+ Great soundtrack.
+ Well-written characters.

Cons:
- The scale of the game is a bit too massive for my taste. Trimming both maps down by about 25%—along with a corresponding reduction in main and side quests—would have actually benefited the overall experience.
- Despite having played the first game, it still took some time to learn the ropes. Without looking up a few things online, I would have never figured out certain mechanics, which would have made for a pretty tedious playthrough.
- While the combat system has its merits, it can also be incredibly frustrating at times.
- It relies heavily on the classic open-world formula. Sometimes it just feels like you're ticking off markers on a map.
- Towards the end of the game, I had an epic fight against an antagonist. I was probably underleveled, but I found a reliable way to counter his attacks. I successfully pulled off over 45 (!) counters and still couldn't defeat him. That was honestly just absurd and completely pulled me out of the immersion.

50+ hours in and this is already one of my favourite games OF ALL TIME. 

Playing KCD2 feels as close as I will get to living out my dream of being a proper Medieval knight.

Storyline is fantastic - there are so many twists and turns that I am already looking forward to my second playthrough before I have even finished my first...  

The Landscape and environments are beautiful, which makes it insanely immersive.

Combat is really tricky and almost frustrating at first - I was dying a LOT - but after watching a couple of youtube tutorials, it makes a lot more sense. (Don't spam ripostes, learn the masterstrike, and keep an eye on your stamina most of all) Once you wrap your head around it, and get good, it is incredibly satisfying. 

Oh and by the way, the game is super optimised, I am running it on my old 1080, and it is running beautifully. 

Just get this game already, it's a masterpiece.

These games are very unique to me. I haven't played a game like this where I felt I could run around and do anything I want since the fallout and skyrim games. The different armors and weapons are quite fun to mess around with. The crafting aspect of the game was a little slow for my liking at first but when I started to understand how to do it properly I started enjoying it a lot more. In fact, most of the game was like that for me. There is definitely a learning curve to this game, but since I played the first one some time ago it was a little easier for me to get how to do stuff. 

The story was great, the characters were awesome, but even with the first one, I've always been frustrated with the combat. Sometimes my swings will phase through my enemies, the jankiness of fighting multiple enemies, and other stuff I won't bother to mention. The longer I played the game and leveled up, it seems I ended up running into more stronger armored bandits to fight, which means they kept bonking me in the head once and nearly killing me, even with my very high armor. It kind of reminded me of Obilivon where you get a high enough level all the bandits have deadric armor. Though I have to say when you get into the flow of a fight it can be insanely satisfying. 

In the end, loved this game.

Just finished the story (｡・ω・｡)

An absolute masterpiece, definitely one of the best RPG games that I have ever played. The storyline was beautifully developed and very immersive. There is just so much attention to detail and historical accuracy; I am out of words to describe how epic the whole journey was. 

 Everything about this game was so realistic-  to the point that it is almost a medieval simulator. I really enjoyed the first person sword-fighting, as well as going around and collecting exquisite armor. This game pulls you into all aspects of medieval life - the taverns, stealing, gambling, brawling, everything ~  

Visibly, a lot of work was put into optimizing the graphics of this game. The scenery was beautiful to the point that just travelling around and sightseeing was extremely satisfying. 

 The only downside of this game was that since it was too realistic, early game grinding was really hard and slow-paced unless you knew what you were doing (e.g. searching for tutorials and playthroughs online, etc.). The game itself doesn't really give enough hints on what to do, so initially it does feel like you're playing medieval beggar simulator.  However, this may have been intentional for historical accuracy, as the creators of this game probably wanted players to experience how tough medieval life was. So this game may not be for everyone. Nevertheless, everything after early-game was absolute peak. 

There are also some mods that should definitely be installed to improve the experience of this game, such as the unlimited saving mod (this game does not have auto-save, so you might accidentally lose hours of playtime if you play in vanilla, which can be very frustrating). 

Overall, this game was so much fun! I enjoyed the entire story ~ 9.5/10

Thank you warhorse studios for the amazing experience (≧∀≦)ゞ

citations.review_text: combat is actually awful. block promt>1/5 chance it works... you have the stamina of a wheelchair bound toddler. your armor and weapons can be 10 times better then the npcs yet you take 3-5 hits to die and they take 47. they can block as much as they want... you can block maybe 3 times. you also go through a pair of shoes daily.....................

Great story and gameplay! Very good graphics, it runs smooth!
The combo fight system is quite clunky and intransparent and needs improvement.
It's a very good game, and love the story line.  Combat is a bit of a pain, but nonetheless, I love how detailed and immersive the game is.

These games are very unique to me. I haven't played a game like this where I felt I could run around and do anything I want since the fallout and skyrim games. The different armors and weapons are quite fun to mess around with. The crafting aspect of the game was a little slow for my liking at first but when I started to understand how to do it properly I started enjoying it a lot more. In the end, loved this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as highly detailed and reactive, with non-player characters following daily routines and responding to the player's actions and reputation.

citations.review_text:
I tried the first game years ago, but I never got very far before giving up. Then I saw how much better Kingdom Come: Deliverance II looked, so I grabbed it during a sale.

Best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decision ever.

I’m writing this while I’m still in what feels like the early game, and I’m already completely addicted.

At one point, I honestly thought:

“Wait... is this really the end of the introduction?”

Because I had already spent dozens of hours playing. Then I finished the wedding, got captured, got tortured, and suddenly realized:

“Oh... so THIS is where the real game actually begins.”

What the hell have I been doing all this time?!

Well...

Helping random villagers.
Learning new skills.
Exploring every corner of the map.
Getting distracted by every side quest I walked past.
Playing dice for way longer than any reasonable person should.
And every night... “recovering” the money I spent on training by quietly taking it back. 😂

Seriously, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dangerous if you’re easily distracted.

The world feels incredibly alive. NPCs actually have personalities, daily routines, and their own little stories. Many of them even show up again later. I found myself remembering people not because of their names, but because of what they did or what happened between us.

The choices are also much more interesting than I expected. They aren’t always just “good” or “evil.” Sometimes you genuinely try to do the right thing, think you made the best possible choice...

And then everything goes horribly wrong anyway.

Combat is still unforgiving, exactly as it should be. Even after becoming much stronger, Henry never turns into some unstoppable superhero. Make one stupid mistake or let a few enemies surround you, and you’re still completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥.

And yes...

I may have spent an unreasonable amount of time collecting special dice instead of saving the kingdom.

No regrets. The kingdom can wait. I need my lucky dice.

Also, my English isn’t great, but don’t let that stop you fro…

[h1]Kingdom Come: Deliverance II - A Living World Like No Other[/h1]
[hr][/hr]

81 hours. Main story done, all side quests and missions in Trosky region, all quests 
in Kuttenberg city itself, and a good chunk of the smaller towns around Kuttenberg. 
Did I do absolutely everything? No. But I did a lot. And I feel good about where I 
stopped.

By the end I was starting to feel a bit drained and the combat was getting too easy, 
so I wrapped up the main story and called it. The game gave me 81 
hours of content and I loved basically all of it.

[h2]The World is Insane[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

I can barely think of another game that makes the world feel this alive. Like 
genuinely alive. NPCs have homes they go back to. They sleep. They eat. They talk to 
their neighbours about their day. You walk through a town and people are just... 
living their lives. It sounds simple but almost no game actually does this at this 
level of detail.

And the way the world reacts to [b]you specifically[/b] is something else. I won 
boxing tournaments and fighting competitions and then walked through towns and random 
NPCs would recognise me. Some would get nervous and not want to mess with me. Others 
would actually come up and want to test themselves against me just to see if they 
could take me. Word travels. People know who you are and what you've done. That kind 
of dynamic reactivity is rare and it makes the world feel real in a way that's hard 
to explain until you experience it.

[h2]I Was a Loot Goblin and I Regret Nothing[/h2]
[hr][/hr]

Every chest. Every drawer. Every house. Every store. All of it. Looted. I lockpicked 
my way through the entire game and stacked everything onto my horse and sold it all. 
I was basically running a one man criminal empire across medieval Bohemia.

What made it even better is knowing how the NPCs react. These people wake up in the 
morning and their entire house is empty. Everything gone. And they're out there trying 
to figure out who did it while I'm…

Simply a masterpiece. Immersive AF, really cool story, everything can be done in multiple ways and the world reacts accordingly (sneaking, brute-forcing, stealing or going a more noble way, etc.) the fact everything you do grants you more perks on that activity is a constant feeling of progression that makes every activity worth doing and feel rewarding.
Also, certain romancing scene at the end of the game... 10/10

Just finished the story (｡・ω・｡)

An absolute masterpiece, definitely one of the best RPG games that I have ever played. The storyline was beautifully developed and very immersive. There is just so much attention to detail and historical accuracy; I am out of words to describe how epic the whole journey was. 

 Everything about this game was so realistic-  to the point that it is almost a medieval simulator. I really enjoyed the first person sword-fighting, as well as going around and collecting exquisite armor. This game pulls you into all aspects of medieval life - the taverns, stealing, gambling, brawling, everything ~  

Visibly, a lot of work was put into optimizing the graphics of this game. The scenery was beautiful to the point that just travelling around and sightseeing was extremely satisfying. 

 The only downside of this game was that since it was too realistic, early game grinding was really hard and slow-paced unless you knew what you were doing (e.g. searching for tutorials and playthroughs online, etc.). The game itself doesn't really give enough hints on what to do, so initially it does feel like you're playing medieval beggar simulator.  However, this may have been intentional for historical accuracy, as the creators of this game probably wanted players to experience how tough medieval life was. So this game may not be for everyone. Nevertheless, everything after early-game was absolute peak. 

There are also some mods that should definitely be installed to improve the experience of this game, such as the unlimited saving mod (this game does not have auto-save, so you might accidentally lose hours of playtime if you play in vanilla, which can be very frustrating). 

Overall, this game was so much fun! I enjoyed the entire story ~ 9.5/10

Thank you warhorse studios for the amazing experience (≧∀≦)ゞ

claims.claim: Reviewers note that hardcore difficulty removes features and increases tedium by eliminating fast travel, stripping UI elements, and imposing save limits.

citations.review_text:
If you've played the first game in the series, this improves on nearly everything from that mold. The story and gameplay are great. The cutscenes are great. There is a lot of care put into the things you get to see and the world begins to feel lived in by the characters around you.

Both games in this series are as good of a 'medieval themed' RPG as I've engaged with and I thoroughly enjoyed what they put together. 

For all the work they put into castle and siege mechanics I wish they could have squeezed some more out of it rather than a few relatively short quests, but I guess we'll see these features in their future games.

Something I really want to push back on is their take on 'hardcore difficulty' which I hate. Their idea is to remove features of a game, which in doing so makes your experience worse. No fast travel, too much UI removal, more save limits... the list goes on.

Some developers, and not just Warhorse Studios, think players want to to quadruple their playtime and turn minor tasks in a [i] videogame [/i] into something akin to a chore rather than making combat more difficult for players.

Barring that complaint, if you want to jump into a Looter/Combat RPG I personally haven't touched many games like this that are as good or better.

By far one of the best games ever. The product of graphics, gameplay, and an interesting medieval plot (like in no other game) make it a masterpiece. Before starting the game, i couldn't decide whether to play on standard or hardcore difficulty. I read some reviews that said that the game becomes way too easy after some time, so I chose hardcore. (as a person that finished KCD1) However, as a person that already finished the game I can tell that the game becomes a lot easier no matter what the difficulty is. It remains constantly difficult only if you literally avoid every side quest and simply follow the campaign without paying attention to anything else. When I got to Kuttenberg and participated in tournaments, my character became so strong that I could easily kill the whole Sigismund camp if I wanted, and I'm not a pro at all. It's all considering that I played with a debuff that stole 40% of all the experience I got from any activity. Thus, I recommend to play on standard difficulty, since the main difference is that you can't fast travel and you get 3 debuffs that are significant only in the 1st 15-20 hours of the game. Standard difficulty will let you fully enjoy every quest and avoid unnecessary complications that only worsen the experience. The last thing I want to mention is DLC, and you MUST buy them to extend the joy of playing for extra 15-20+ hours. (except the one with the brushes) I personally got the most joy thanks to them. 
Thus, I recommend this game a lot and advise you to play on standard difficulty with DLC to maximize satisfaction from every quest.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as challenging and requiring practice, timing, and skill development to master over time.

citations.review_text:
Despite me being ♥♥♥♥ at combat in the beginning of both games, everything else kept me hooked and made me want to get better. The charatcers are lovely, the VA's are super talented and the performance capture is amazing! Coming straight from the frist game the performance capture in this really blew my mind, the scenes felt so real with the facial expressions and body language. And the story really kept me on my toes, so many twists and turns my naive mind dind't see coming. 

The romance with a certain lord was really beautiful, it was done so well and I'm so glad for that. A proper slow burn with a satisfying "end".

Best RPG I ever played, it makes you play consciously throughout the whole game, no time for autopilot. You didnt listen to the NPC and give a random answer? your reputation drops. The combat is something you have to get used to but its not as bad as most people say, if you understand it its a great way to fight and simulate actual duels. 
Also the only RPG I have ever finished there is nothing boring about it the story is great. 

Only bad thing I can think of is the armor scaling, at some point if you do a lot of sidequests or find very good armor you just dont upgrade for 30 hours playtime. Overall great Immersive RPG.

I just finished kingdom come deliverance 2, I think I have to say that it is tied with rdr2 for my favorite game ive ever played, if you like single player games then you should buy it, My playthrough was 105 hours and there are a ♥♥♥♥ load of side quests that I didnt do, and I did every single one I came across, the voice acting is phenomenal, the story is fantastic. the combat is very fun and takes skill. you can approach basically everything the way you want to. I started as a stealthy archer build and then slowly turned into a knight tank. its absolutly worth the money if you like freeroam RPG play your way games. 10/10. Buy this game, dont think about it, just buy if if you are even remotely interested.

ITS WORTH THE MONEY
This is one of the most, if not, the most amazing game I have ever played. I had low expectations from the start, since people slander this game for being way too hard. Which I felt the same way from the start, considering it goes well into the realistic survival parts, making everything hard at the beginning. Except the hardest part of this game is hands down the combat, but DO NOT BE SCARED OFF you can definitely get the hang of it eventually. Most importantly this games difficulty will make you feel more connected to the story, your character, and feel more rewarding overall. 

Not to mention that the scenery and map in this game is probably the MOST realistic, and has likeness of a real 14th century England. Literally the closest any game could have possibly got it. Beautiful landscapes that all are spread among one of the largest feeling free roam maps as well. I don't wanna spoil how many amazing quirks and details there are that makes it feel that way, but i could go on forever. 

Lastly I would not have kept playing this game if it wasn't for the abundance of side missions and tasks, not to take any shine from the main story. But never have I heard such funny and creative dialogue from npc's and from the main character. Truly makes you feel as if you are in Monty pythons holy grail, with some of the most loveable characters, as well as the most hated. 

Overall, whoever is reading this PLAY THE GAME... PLEASE!!! 
I have put over 170s hours into this game, and I am a casual gamer. Probably took 100 hours just for me to complete the main story. You'll understand why once it sucks you in, and mark my words you will get sucked in. Just a matter of time, but you have to push through the rough learning curve in the start, I BELIEVE IN YOU!

147 hours played

After 147 hours, I can confidently say this game never stopped being fun. There was always something worth doing, whether it was progressing the main story, exploring the world, or getting sidetracked by the amazing side quests.

The story is one of the game’s biggest strengths. It’s rich, engaging, and full of memorable characters. I also loved how it balances serious moments with humor, making the journey feel fresh and entertaining from beginning to end.

The combat system isn’t something you can master overnight. It takes practice, patience, and learning your timing. It can be challenging at first, but once it clicks, every victory feels incredibly satisfying.

The world feels alive, and many of the side quests are just as enjoyable as the main storyline. It’s rare to find an RPG where I genuinely wanted to experience almost everything the game had to offer.

I truly enjoyed every minute of my 147-hour journey. If you’re looking for an immersive RPG with a fantastic story, memorable humor, and a rewarding combat system, this game is an easy recommendation.

One of the best RPGs I’ve ever played.

KCD 3 ?. DEFINITELY !!!

Overall a fun experience that you can lay hundreds of ours into and not even realize it. Spent a lot of my time immersing myself in each region, town, and scenery. The combat is different from most RPGS, difficult at first, yet easily accomplished through experience and time.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that side quests feature deep investigative elements and variable outcomes based on player actions.

citations.review_text:
It is an amazing historical medieval RPG and I love the bits of it that are lovable, I also hate the bits of it that have not been upgraded from the last game, and the bits that lack any kind of depth and polishing. 
I don't think I have ever played another RPG, where you can try to talk reason into a person, and once they disagree, strangle them unconscious, steal all their items and clothes, or even kill them and then be able to advance the quest, sometimes with amazing changes to the quest storyline and very possibly never get reprimanded for this in any way.
 The way that there is no black and white moral system in the game is amazing. I've never played another RPG where every single character has a voice, and there is an unimaginable amount of dialog in this game. Not only the main quest, but majority of the side quests have amazing depth, investigating the serial killings in Kuttenberg with all of it's different corpse examinations, gathering evidence and talking to suspects is simply amazing.
But the downside of this is, that some sidequests are very short, feel detached and completely  irrelevant, with no choice to be made. Basically many of the shorter quests feel like they're  filling some kind of a quota paper at the office "quest 231, it's done, next", the side quest a Damsel in Distress is a good example of this. On the other hand you have quests where you can investigate things, make different kinds of observations based on skill, and situations where Henry with high level speech and scholar can make different observations and see through lies. But then all of a sudden you have quests where you can make no choices and your level 30 Proto-Sherlock Holmes Henry, suddenly falls into a very obvious trap. This game has some timed quests, where it doesn't make any mention of the quest being timed or there being a sense of hurry, and so if you have some other things going on at the moment, you might get the worst possible ending for a quest by just not doing …

I remember booting up KCD2 expecting a bigger, prettier version of the first game. What I got was something that pulled me in and did not let go. One moment I am riding through the countryside just to see what is over the next hill, and the next I am three hours deep into a side quest I never planned on starting. It has that same soul the first game had, just polished to a point I did not think was possible. Bohemia in KCD2 does not feel like a game map. It feels like a place. The villages have their own rhythm, the forests feel like you could actually get lost in them, and Kuttenberg is easily one of the most impressive cities I have walked through in an RPG. Henry's story grabs you early and it never really lets go, and the way KCD2 treats Czech history gives the whole thing a weight most games do not even attempt. What surprised me most was how much the small things added up. Just riding back to camp after a long day, with nothing but the music playing, ended up being one of my favorite parts of the game, and that music never once felt like background noise. Combat still has that same bite from the first game, but it is smoother now, easier to pick up if you want to keep things simple, or deep enough to master if you want real combos. Side activities like alchemy and blacksmithing pulled me in more than I expected too. 

KCD2 is not perfect. NPCs sometimes forget something happened right after a quest ends, the pacing dips depending on how you play, and Mutt got nerfed, which still stings a little. None of that changed how much I enjoyed the ride though.

As for the DLCs, the first one brings in a mysterious painter character and a string of fetch quests with a surprisingly dark undertone, and it fits nicely into the main story if you run them side by side. The second is more of a quality of life add-on. You finally get a home base with your own customizable forge to craft and rest at, though the quests tied to it can feel a bit repetitive after a while. The …

I don't review many games but had to drop a positive review for KCD2. Its the first single player game that was easy to keep coming back to, even after breaks. 

First started Nov 2025 and just finished the main story, just about every side quest, and 1 DLC at end of June 2026. Didn't quite have the drive to finish the blacksmith DLC but I'd say I got everything I wanted out of it.

I'd recommend to anyone that likes a Story RPG that they're ok with Sinking 80+ hours into

It also scales well to lower end hardware without looking like a complete turd so its easily accessible

one of the greatest games of all time without a doubt. coming from KCD1 especially, the increase in quality across the board was so staggering that it made me burst out laughing. the entire package here is such a joy to experience, from the quests, the combat, the general tedium of daily life in bohemia, the characters, the graphics (and well-optimized!), the environments, the MUSIC, the sound design, the history (if you're interested). i will cherish the time i spent with this game forever, and its memory will live on as i listen to the soundtracks during my workday. 

I did have to upgrade my ram (32gb up from 16) when I got to Kuttenberg. played at 1440p on high settings at a shockingly consistent 75fps+.

this is one of the best games ive ever played its got a few bugs but not bugs that are an inconvinece, this game should be worth slightly more than its on the steam page, you do have to listen a lot to what the npc say or you might feel lost.
amazing storie and i love the armor, architecture and atencion to small details, my pc is kinda bad so i have to keep everything on low and still the game looks beutiful.

Sadly, it misses the mark. It has all the necessary ingredients to be a great game, on par with Witcher 3 or RDR2, but no. In the end it feels just too mechanical and clunky. Quests are too cliche, characters are too bland, itemisation is uninspiring, and so on. And don't let me start about the combat mechanics - it's just plain awful.

It has the best possible open world implementation in RPGs that I have ever seen though. The game is visually beautiful AND well optimised at the same time. Probably, because it's built on Cryengine and not on UE5.  

I would give it a thumb up if the main quest line wasn't so long and tedious. Pity.

citations.review_text:
Jumped straight into Kingdom Come: Deliverance II without playing the first one, and it instantly became one of my favorite RPGs of all time. I’m currently on my 5th playthrough and nearly maxed out in everything.

The Good:
Hardcore Mode is Peak Immersion: I have zero direction sense and got lost more times than I can count, but not having a map indicator forces you to actually pay attention to the world. Put on a good pair of headphones and just listen—the sound design (from shoes crunching on gravel to rustling bushes while sneaking) is top tier. Playing with all negative perks enabled was easily my favorite run.

Insane Freedom & Replayability: The choice design is mind-blowing. You can be a savior or a killer, a saint or a thief. (Pro-tip: Being a super nice guy who secretly steals everything makes life hilariously easy). Seeing how small choices ripple out into dialogue, trading, and story beats kept all 5 runs feeling fresh.

Mastering the Mechanics: The learning curves for combat, speech, and stealth aren't annoying—they're fun challenges. Going from struggling with basic mechanics to mastering every playstyle (especially archery, gathering, and stealing) feels incredibly earned.

Unmatched Story: The narrative hooked me from the start. Without spoiling anything: the betrayals will shock you.

The Bad:
Kuttenberg Tournament Bugs: The game does glitch periodically, and the Kuttenberg tournament is by far the most frustrating part. It likes to bug out after matches (sometimes making you fight again after winning, or marking a loss when the opponent surrendered without touching you). Save after every single round!

Pro-Tips for Beginners:
Put your money in the chest at the very beginning before the lake ambush (you can pick it up later!).

Get your horse ASAP.

Get the good old Pebbles perk: Ride your horse for 30 kilometers (no fast travel!) to unlock it—the stats are the absolute best.
